scope: Historic coaching inn core with granite walls, pitched roofs, chimneys and entry; exclude modern hotel extensions.

originalReview.notes: The named photographer brianp3d CC0courtyard view confirms the granite museum/stables range, long hipped rag-slate roof, four low eaves dormers with paired left opening, gabled entrance porch, dark divided windows and low connector to the slate-clad bar visible along the right side. Current model preserves those proportions, opening hierarchy, perpendicular courtyard relationship and physical slate/stone/timber surfaces. The full fixed historic inn envelope is retained: five-window bar, twin axial stacks, museum range, attached rear range and low historic east connector. The main bar front and twin stacks are supported by the already recorded HistoricEngland architectural description; the photo crops that front. Hidden rear elevations, roof joins, heights, exact masonry, chimney details and low connector openings remain conservative mapped/description-led medium-fi estimates. Full exterior accepted at the agreed approximate scope, without signs, temporary furniture or interiors. Modern long east hotel/far rear service wings remain outside the original scope. Original map, terrain and placement are unchanged.
